Finding your way around the console

The screen at a glance#

Area Where What it is for
Top bar Across the top Product name, active ADOM, environment and HA badges, the device switcher, Switch Product, Tools, Search, the notifications bell and your user menu.
Sidebar Left The menu of the ADOM you are in. Groups expand and collapse; the group holding the current page opens by itself.
Content Centre The page. Confirmation and error messages appear at its top.
Bookmarks rail Right edge (star tab) Your own filing of devices and links. See Bookmarks.
Footer Bottom Product, version and the Concept Map link.

The menu icon at the far left of the top bar (Toggle sidebar) hides or shows the sidebar.

Wide tables and row actions#

Tables use the full width of the content area and are fitted to it at every desktop width (from 769 px; phones keep their own horizontal scroll). When a table is wider than the screen, SATOM takes these steps in order, and stops as soon as the table fits:

  1. Text wraps between words. Headers and ordinary text cells may take two lines. Names, badges, numbers, dates, checkboxes and actions stay on one line.
  2. Very long values are shortened. A certificate, an image or a message body shows on one line with an ellipsis; hover over it to read the full value.
  3. The least useful columns are hidden, starting from the right. The name column, the checkbox, Status and Actions are never hidden, and never more than half of the columns. A link above the table says N columns hidden · Show all (hover over it to see which). Show all brings them back and the table scrolls inside its own box; All columns shown · Fit to width hides them again. The choice is not kept when you leave the page.
  4. As a last resort, long words in text cells may break anywhere.

A table that already fits is not changed. The fit is worked out again when you resize the window, open a tab or collapse the sidebar.

Row actions stay on one line. Rows show their two or three main actions as buttons; the rest are in the … menu (More actions) at the end of the row. Lists with this menu include Appliances, Plugin Studio, Deep monitors, Service Monitor, Report Studio and API Tokens. Toolbars above a list (the device GUI pages, the Lua editor, Transaction Tracer, the appliance page, Thresholds) also stay on one line.

In Plugin Studio, below 1400 px wide the Explorer becomes a strip of tabs above the table, so the table gets the full width.

The top bar#

Product name and badges#

  • Brand — the SATOM mark and product title. Clicking it opens the home page of the current ADOM.
  • ADOM: — the active administrative domain, colour-coded (Global blue, FortiWeb red, FortiADC green, FortiAuthenticator purple, FortiAnalyzer amber, FortiGate teal). It is always visible so an ADOM change is never silent.
  • PRODUCTION / DEVELOPMENT — the environment set by an administrator in Settings → General → Environment.
  • PRIMARY / STANDBY — shown only on a high-availability installation; tells you which node you are on. The standby is read-only.

Device switcher#

In the FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer ADOMs the centre of the top bar shows the selected device (Zone, Line, Dept, Host). Click it to open Switch device, pick an appliance, and it becomes the context for every per-device page of that ADOM. The selection is kept per ADOM. If an ADOM holds exactly one appliance you can see, that appliance is used automatically.

💡Tip

In the FortiWeb ADOM, opening a per-device page (for example Device Backups or WAF Artifacts) with no device selected takes you to the Service Diagram so you can pick one first.

Switch Product#

The product logo with two arrows opens the product chooser (Select the product you want to manage). Choose a card and click Open →. See ADOMs and products.

Tools menu#

The wrench icon (Tools) opens a menu available on every page:

Entry Opens
Regex calculator, Regex cheat sheet, Pattern library The regex lab. See Regex Lab.
Network calculator A subnet calculator.
Certificate inspector See Certificate inspector.
False-positive explainer See False-positive explainer.
Report a problem A form (Title, Description, Send report) sent to the administrators. The current page address and your browser are attached automatically.
Release Notes Every device ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer); not in Global. See Release notes.
Bug Reports Administrators only (users.manage); the inbox of submitted reports, with a red counter of open ones. See Bug reports inbox.

The transaction tracer left this menu on 2026-10-16: it is a page under Operations → Troubleshooting. See Transaction tracer.

More in Tools menu.

Bug reports inbox#

Report a problem is open to everyone: fill in Title (required) and Description and click Send report. The page confirms "Thanks — your report was sent to the administrators." (an empty title is refused with "Please enter a short title for the problem.").

Every active administrator gets a bell notification "New bug report: "</em>; administrators who opted in also get an email. In <strong>Bug Reports</strong> (URL <code>/reports</code>, also in the <strong>Administrator</strong> group of the Global ADOM) an administrator sees the open reports and the 50 most recently resolved ones, and resolves a report with an optional note — the page confirms <em>"Report marked as resolved. The reporter has been notified."</em> and the reporter receives the notification <em>"Your bug report was resolved"</em>.</p> <h3 id="search">Search<a class="dc-anchor" href="#search" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>The magnifier opens fleet-wide <a href="search.html">Search</a>. It is shown in the Global, FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs to users who can open Search (any <em>view</em> permission, for example <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#appliances-view" title="View appliances — See the appliance inventory"><code>appliances.view</code></a>). The FortiAnalyzer ADOM has no magnifier; use <strong>Operations → Search</strong> there.</p> <p><strong>Keyboard shortcut:</strong> on any page that shows the magnifier, press <code>/</code> (while the cursor is not in a text field) to open Search. On the Search page itself, <code>/</code> focuses the search box.</p> <h3 id="notifications-bell">Notifications bell<a class="dc-anchor" href="#notifications-bell" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>Shows a red counter of unread notifications and a drop-down with the 8 most recent. <strong>Clear</strong> marks them read (they stay on the page); <strong>View all notifications ›</strong> opens the full list. The counter refreshes every 30 seconds. See <a href="notifications.html">Notifications</a>.</p> <h3 id="user-menu">User menu<a class="dc-anchor" href="#user-menu" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>Your initial and username, top right:</p> <ul> <li>the header shows your username and role;</li> <li><strong>Profile</strong> — your personal preferences;</li> <li><strong>Language</strong> — jumps to the language card, showing your current code;</li> <li><strong>Sign Out</strong>.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="first-login.html#your-profile-page">First login</a>.</p> <h2 id="the-sidebar">The sidebar<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-sidebar" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <p>The sidebar is different in each ADOM, but the groups SATOM adds around a device's own menu are defined once and drawn in the same order in every ADOM. Four rules decide what you see:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Your permissions come first.</strong> Groups you are not entitled to are <strong>not shown</strong>. The <strong>Administrator</strong> group needs the administrator capability (<a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a>) and <strong>Automation</strong> needs write access (any permission that grants configuration writes, such as <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#appliances-edit" title="Edit appliances — Add, edit or delete appliances"><code>appliances.edit</code></a>). Inside a group, an entry is shown only when you can open that page: the sidebar asks the same permission the page enforces, so a link never leads to <em>Access denied</em>. Every page still checks your permissions itself.</li> <li><strong>Greyed out, not missing.</strong> In a device ADOM, an entry whose page does not work for that product is drawn greyed out with a slash icon and no link. Hover it to read why, for example <em>Not available for FortiGate: the WAF pages read FortiWeb web-protection objects.</em> <strong>Path Diagnostics</strong> is drawn the same way when an administrator has switched it off (<em>Path Diagnostics is switched off for this site (Settings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics → Availability).</em>).</li> <li><strong>A move never takes a page away.</strong> When an entry moved to a group your profile cannot see, it stays where it was for you. See <a href="#when-your-profile-cannot-see-a-group">When your profile cannot see a group</a>.</li> <li><strong>An administrator can declutter it.</strong> Entries, submenus and groups unticked in <strong>Settings → User Interface → Appearance → Sidebar menu</strong> are not drawn for anybody, in any ADOM. The page itself is not blocked: a direct link still opens it if your profile allows it. See <a href="appearance.html">Appearance</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Every link in the sidebar carries a star: click it to add the page to your <strong>Favourites</strong>. See <a href="bookmarks.html">Bookmarks</a>.</p> <p><strong>Where you are.</strong> The page you are on is drawn with a light band, a bold label and an amber bar on its left. Every menu and submenu above it keeps a bold label and an amber icon, so the path to the page reads at a glance even when a branch is folded. Menus, submenus and entries all use the same type size; a menu is told apart by its bold label. A label too long for the sidebar ends in an ellipsis (<em>Agentless VPN Personal Bookm…</em>). A Plugin Studio app, whose name its author chooses, wraps to up to three lines instead; a longer name ends in an ellipsis and shows whole when you hover the entry, and its favourite star stays clear of the text.</p> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed in 2.11.0:</strong> Appliances moved from the Administrator group to the Global / Fleet group, so operators reach it from the menu; the shortcut <code>/</code> opens Search from every page; and sidebar entries are hidden when your profile cannot open the page.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed in 3.1.0:</strong> the menu order is the same in every ADOM. <strong>Appliances</strong> moved to <strong>Administrator</strong>; <strong>Schema builds</strong>, <strong>Build compatibility</strong> and <strong>Certificate Manager</strong> moved to <strong>Automation</strong>; the Global <strong>Studio</strong> group became a sub-menu at the foot of <strong>Administrator</strong>; the Fleet group was reordered (Dashboard where the ADOM has one, then Jobs, Monitoring, Calendar, Architecture, Service Diagram, Search, DNS Lookup). Every device ADOM draws the device's own menu (FortiAnalyzer when a layout exists for its build) plus the same Fleet, Operations, API, Automation, Administrator and Plugins groups as FortiWeb, and the foot of the sidebar no longer links the documentation or the API console. A profile that cannot see the new group keeps the entry where it was.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-14:</strong> <strong>Fleet</strong> holds a <strong>Troubleshooting</strong> sub-menu in every ADOM, with <strong>Backend Reachability</strong>, <strong>Config Compare</strong>, <strong>Path Diagnostics</strong> and <strong>Scout</strong>; the Troubleshooting sub-menu under <strong>Operations</strong> and the flat entries in the Global block are gone. Fleet now runs Dashboard (where the ADOM has one), Calendar, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring, Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting, then Fleet Objects and WAF (FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs only) and Jobs last. Three labels changed: the fault-localisation ladder formerly called <strong>Scout</strong> is <strong>Path Diagnostics</strong>; the AI assistant formerly called <strong>AI Advisor</strong> is <strong>Scout</strong>; the firmware release-notes reviewer formerly shown as <strong>Scout</strong> is the <strong>Upgrade Advisory</strong>. Addresses and bookmarks are unchanged. In the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs the sub-menu holds <strong>Scout</strong> only: the other three work on FortiWeb and FortiADC objects.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-14 (later the same day):</strong> the <strong>Fleet</strong> group is gone. Its entries open the <strong>Operations</strong> group, which is now the first group of every device ADOM, above Device Backups, Diagnose Log Collection and Import Backup; the device's own menu follows it. The <strong>API</strong> group became a sub-menu of <strong>Automation</strong> (<strong>Automation → API → Registry & console</strong>); a profile with <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#registry-view" title="View registry — Browse the endpoint registry & API explorer"><code>registry.view</code></a> but without write access keeps the standalone <strong>API</strong> group. Every entry kept its own permission. The Global ADOM is unchanged.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Diagnose Log Collection moved on 2026-10-14 (later still).</strong> It is no longer one of the Operations group's own entries. It is the last entry of <strong>Operations → Troubleshooting</strong>, in all five device ADOMs, where it runs that ADOM's diagnostic battery. Administrators choose the battery under the new <strong>Administrator → Diagnostic Battery</strong> entry. The Global ADOM shows neither entry in its menu.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-14 (evening):</strong> the Global ADOM draws <strong>Automation</strong> as a sub-menu of its <strong>Global</strong> block, above Jobs, instead of a group of its own. <strong>Administrator</strong> is split into sections — <strong>Access</strong>, <strong>Change Management</strong>, <strong>Devices</strong>, <strong>Objects</strong>, <strong>Studio</strong> and <strong>System</strong> — and both the sections and their entries are in alphabetical order in the language you use the console in. A section with no entry you may open is not drawn. In a device ADOM, <strong>Python Console</strong> moved into <strong>Administrator → Studio</strong> (since the release after 3.3.7 it is part of <strong>Plugin Studio</strong>, together with the Script Library). No entry changed its permission.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-14 (late evening):</strong> <strong>System Automations</strong> moved from <strong>Automation</strong> to <strong>Administrator → System</strong>, in every ADOM. <strong>Automation</strong> keeps <strong>Automations</strong>, which now also holds the operator actions (upgrade preparation, firmware upgrade, reboot, HA failover, certificate renewals, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep, Custom REST call) and is live in every ADOM except FortiGate. <strong>Schema builds</strong> and <strong>Build compatibility</strong> moved into the <strong>API</strong> sub-menu of <strong>Automation</strong>; the Global ADOM now has an API sub-menu with just those two pages. No entry changed its permission. See <a href="scheduled-actions.html">Scheduled actions</a>.</p> </div> <h3 id="global-adom">Global ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#global-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Group</th> <th>Entries</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Global</strong></td> <td>Wiki<em>, Dashboard, Calendar</em>, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring (Fleet health → SATOM health, Device health · Sentinel<em> · Metrics · Analysis · Deep monitors · Service Monitor · Analytics · Reports), Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting (Backend Reachability, Config Compare, HTTP Observatory, Path Diagnostics, Scout</em>), Automation<em> (alphabetical: API (Schema builds</em>, Build compatibility<em>), Automations, Certificate Manager</em>, Change Requests<em>), Plugins (All plugins</em>, Report Studio<em>, Lua Studio</em>, then one entry per published app you may use), Jobs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>ADOMs</strong></td> <td>One link per active product ADOM</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Plugin Studio</strong>*</td> <td>A first-level entry, not a group: apps (flow and script), console, data stores, connections, API Catalog, examples</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Administrator</strong>*</td> <td>In sections, alphabetical: Access (API Tokens<em>, Audit Log</em>, Groups, Users) · Devices (Appliances, Device Console, Device Provisioning) · Objects (AppIDs, Classification, DNS Resolvers, Line Profiles, Stored Assets) · System (Bug Reports, Collection, Container operations*, Database, DNS Lookup)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p><strong>Global</strong> is a fixed block at the top, not a collapsible group. Its <strong>Troubleshooting</strong> sub-menu is the same one every device ADOM draws in <strong>Operations</strong>; Sentinel and SATOM health exist in the Global ADOM only. <strong>Fleet Objects</strong> and <strong>WAF</strong> are not in the Global ADOM's menu (they belong to the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs); their pages still open from a bookmark. <strong>Automation</strong> is a sub-menu of the Global block, with <strong>Plugins</strong> right below it and Jobs after them, as in Operations in a device ADOM; its entries are alphabetical in the console's language. Its <strong>API</strong> sub-menu holds <strong>Schema builds</strong> and <strong>Build compatibility</strong> only (the Global ADOM has no device console). <strong>System Automations</strong> is under <strong>Administrator → System</strong>. <strong>Certificate Manager</strong> is under <strong>Automation</strong> in every ADOM (in a device ADOM, Operations › Automation): live in Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC, greyed out with the reason in FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator. The Global ADOM has no device menu; its <strong>Plugins</strong> sub-menu shows <strong>All plugins</strong> to users who also see Automation, and Report Studio, Lua Studio and the <a href="studio-apps.html">Plugin Studio apps</a> published for Global to whoever may open them. It is not drawn when it would be empty.</p> <h3 id="device-adoms-the-shared-groups">Device ADOMs: the shared groups<a class="dc-anchor" href="#device-adoms-the-shared-groups" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>The five device ADOMs (FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer) draw the <strong>device's own menu</strong>, measured on its firmware build, inside the same frame of SATOM groups. From top to bottom:</p> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Group</th> <th>Entries</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>‹ Global</strong></td> <td>Back to the Global ADOM</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Device</strong></td> <td>The selected device (click to switch), or <em>Select a device</em>. A device registered for one of the appliance's own ADOMs shows <em>ADOM: <name></em> beneath it.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Operations</strong></td> <td>Wiki<em>, Calendar</em>, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring (Fleet health → Device health · Metrics · Analysis · Deep monitors · Service Monitor · Analytics · Reports), Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting (Backend Reachability, Config Compare, HTTP Observatory, Path Diagnostics, Scout<em>, Diagnose Log Collection</em>; only Scout<em> and Diagnose Log Collection</em> in the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs), Fleet Objects and WAF (Overview, Inventory, Profiles, Coverage, Artifacts, Exceptions, Search Attack ID, Exceptions & Signature, WAF Artifacts → Object types, Inventory, Device audit) in the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs only, then Device Backups<em>, Import Backup</em>, Template Library<em>, Automation</em> (alphabetical: API (Registry & console<em>, Schema builds</em>, Build compatibility<em>), Automations, Certificate Manager</em>, Change Requests<em>, Mass Deploy</em> (FortiWeb; disabled with the reason in the other device ADOMs), Migration Report<em>, Upgrade Flow</em>), Plugins (Custom Views, Report Studio<em>, Lua Studio</em>, then one entry per published <a href="studio-apps.html">Plugin Studio app</a> you may use in this ADOM), Jobs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong><em>Device menu</em></strong></td> <td>A group named after the product: the device's own menu. See each ADOM below.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Plugin Studio</strong>*</td> <td>A first-level entry, not a group</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Administrator</strong>*</td> <td>In sections, alphabetical: Access (API Tokens<em>, Audit Log</em>, Groups, Users) · Devices (Appliances, Capacity Limits, Device Console, Device Provisioning, Diagnostic Battery*, Firmware, Signatures, System Provisioning) · Objects (DNS Resolvers, Naming, Network Segments, Stored Assets, Template Library) · System (Collection, Database, DNS Lookup)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>The FortiGate ADOM's Operations group also starts with <strong>Dashboard</strong>. Python Console, Report Studio and Lua Studio are scoped to the ADOM you are in. The Python console is a pane of <strong>Plugin Studio</strong>, a first-level entry of the sidebar in every ADOM; Report Studio and Lua Studio are in <strong>Plugins</strong> in every ADOM (in Global: <strong>Global → Plugins</strong>, right below Automation).</p> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-25 (4.0.0):</strong> the <strong>Change Management</strong> section of <strong>Administrator</strong> is gone with the <a href="process.html">Process section</a> (removed). <em>Change Types</em> is now <strong>Change Mgt Types</strong> under <strong>Administrator → Objects</strong> (page title <em>Change Management Types</em>), and <strong>Triggers</strong> is the third tab of <strong>Automation → Automations</strong>, next to <em>Scheduled</em> and <em>On a trigger</em> (administrators only; the address <code>/administration/triggers/</code> is unchanged).</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-24:</strong> <strong>Device Provisioning</strong> and <strong>System Provisioning</strong> moved from <strong>Automation</strong> to <strong>Administrator → Devices</strong>, in every ADOM, with the same rules as before (System Provisioning live in FortiWeb, greyed out in the other device ADOMs, not drawn in Global). Device Provisioning is drawn only while a hypervisor is registered and enabled in Settings → Hypervisors, even when Settings → Appearance has it ticked. Users without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a>, who have no Administrator group, still find both in <strong>Automation</strong>. No permission changed.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-23 (later):</strong> <strong>Automation</strong> sits right above <strong>Plugins</strong> — in a device ADOM it moved from below WAF to Operations, below Template Library; in the Global ADOM Plugins is no longer a sub-menu inside Automation but the one right below it, for the same users. The entries of Automation are alphabetical in the console's language, as the Administrator sections already were.</p> </div> <div class="dc-co dc-co-note"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">ℹ️</span>Note</p> <p><strong>Changed on 2026-10-23:</strong> <strong>Plugin Studio</strong> left <strong>Administrator → Studio</strong> and is an entry of its own on the first level of the sidebar, just above Administrator, in every ADOM. The <strong>Studio</strong> section is gone; Report Studio and Lua Studio moved to <strong>Plugins</strong> in the Global ADOM too. Nothing changed its permission. In Plugin Studio every plugin is now an app — see <a href="studio-apps.html">Plugin Studio apps</a>.</p> </div> <p>Each entry is <strong>live</strong> only in the ADOMs whose devices its page works for, and greyed out (with the reason) in the others:</p> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Entry</th> <th>Live in</th> <th>Reason shown elsewhere</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Operations → WAF (every entry)</td> <td>FortiWeb (drawn greyed out in FortiADC; not drawn in the other ADOMs)</td> <td>the WAF pages read FortiWeb web-protection objects</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Operations → Troubleshooting → Backend Reachability</td> <td>FortiWeb</td> <td>it tests FortiWeb server policies against their back-ends</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Operations → Troubleshooting → Config Compare</td> <td>FortiWeb</td> <td>it compares FortiWeb server policies</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Operations → Troubleshooting → HTTP Observatory</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC</td> <td>it grades sites published by FortiWeb server policies and FortiADC virtual servers</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Operations → Device Backups</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC</td> <td>SATOM has no configuration-backup transport for this product yet</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Operations → Import Backup</td> <td>FortiWeb</td> <td>the offline parser reads FortiWeb configuration files</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Automation → Upgrade Flow</td> <td>FortiWeb</td> <td>the staged upgrade flow cannot pre-flight and flash this product end to end</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Automation → Migration Report</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate</td> <td>there is no migration catalog for this product</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Automation → Automations</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator</td> <td>no operator automation in the catalog targets this product</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Administrator → Capacity Limits</td> <td>FortiWeb</td> <td>the capacity catalog counts FortiWeb object types</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Administrator → Firmware</td> <td>ADOMs that offer firmware in Settings → ADOMs (by default FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer)</td> <td>firmware image management does not apply to this product</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Administrator → Signatures</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC (opens the FortiADC signature page)</td> <td>SATOM keeps no signature database for this product</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Administrator → System Provisioning</td> <td>FortiWeb (not drawn in the Global ADOM)</td> <td>it composes FortiWeb configuration objects</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Administrator → Template Library</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC</td> <td>the template kinds are FortiWeb and FortiADC objects</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Plugins → Lua Studio</td> <td>FortiWeb, FortiADC</td> <td>this product has no scripting object to deploy to</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>Every other entry is live in every device ADOM; the page behind it lists only that ADOM's devices.</p> <h3 id="entries-that-need-a-permission-of-their-own">Entries that need a permission of their own<a class="dc-anchor" href="#entries-that-need-a-permission-of-their-own" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>Entries marked * in the tables above need more than their group:</p> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Entry</th> <th>Shown when</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Calendar</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a> and have not switched the calendar off for yourself</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Scout (the AI assistant)</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#advisor-use" title="Use Scout — Chat with Scout, the AI assistant: WAF false-positive triage, Lua drafting, report search"><code>advisor.use</code></a> and Scout is configured: switched on with at least one usable provider (<a href="ai-advisor.html#requirements">Scout</a>). Unconfigured it is not drawn, even if Appearance › Sidebar menu has it ticked</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Sentinel (Global ADOM)</td> <td>Sentinel is configured: switched on in Settings → AI → Sentinel and at least one FortiWeb you can see that is not retired (host <code>*.invalid</code>) — the FortiWeb attack log is what it sweeps. Otherwise it is not drawn; a FortiWeb in maintenance still counts</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Device Backups</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#backups-view" title="View backups — List existing backups"><code>backups.view</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Diagnose Log Collection</td> <td>You have write access</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Diagnostic Battery</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Import Backup</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#backups-restore" title="Restore backups — Import Backup (offline parser) and, together with Manage users, the appliance Restore page (vault and live config restore)"><code>backups.restore</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>API → Registry & console</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#registry-view" title="View registry — Browse the endpoint registry & API explorer"><code>registry.view</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Upgrade Flow, Migration Report</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" title="Restore backups — Import Backup (offline parser) and, together with Manage users, the appliance Restore page (vault and live config restore)"><code>backups.restore</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>System Automations, Change Requests, Certificate Manager</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>API → Schema builds</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#registry-view" title="View registry — Browse the endpoint registry & API explorer"><code>registry.view</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>API → Build compatibility</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#registry-edit" title="Edit registry — Modify the endpoint registry"><code>registry.edit</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Audit Log</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#audit-view" title="View audit log — Read the application audit trail"><code>audit.view</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>API Tokens</td> <td>The ADOM offers API tokens (Settings → ADOMs)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Plugin Studio</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#studio-script_library" title="Script Library — Write, test and publish sandboxed Python scripts with a form operators fill in"><code>studio.script_library</code></a> or <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#studio-python_console" title="Python Console — Run sandboxed Python against the app's datasets"><code>studio.python_console</code></a>; each of its two panes needs its own</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Report Studio, Lua Studio</td> <td>You hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#studio-plugin_studio" title="Report Studio — Author custom server-side views (plugins)"><code>studio.plugin_studio</code></a> or <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#studio-lua_studio" title="Lua Studio — Author, lint and deploy device Lua scripts"><code>studio.lua_studio</code></a> respectively</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Container operations</td> <td>SATOM runs as a container installation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <h3 id="when-your-profile-cannot-see-a-group">When your profile cannot see a group<a class="dc-anchor" href="#when-your-profile-cannot-see-a-group" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>These entries are drawn somewhere else when you cannot see the group they normally belong to:</p> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Entry</th> <th>Normally in</th> <th>Without that group you find it in</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Appliances</td> <td>Administrator</td> <td><strong>Operations</strong> (the <strong>Global</strong> block in the Global ADOM), for holders of <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#appliances-view" title="View appliances — See the appliance inventory"><code>appliances.view</code></a> without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>API (Registry & console, Schema builds, Build compatibility)</td> <td>Automation → API</td> <td>A standalone <strong>API</strong> group in a device ADOM, and an <strong>API</strong> sub-menu inside the <strong>Global</strong> block in the Global ADOM, for profiles without write access (no Automation menu); each entry keeps its own permission</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Collection</td> <td>Administrator</td> <td>The end of <strong>Operations → Monitoring</strong>, for users with write access but without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Device Console</td> delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Device Provisioning, System Provisioning</td> <td>Administrator → Devices</td> <td><strong>Automation</strong> (Operations › Automation in a device ADOM), for users with write access but without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Template Library</td> <td>Administrator</td> <td><strong>Operations</strong> (device ADOMs), for holders of <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#operations-view" title="View operations — See provisioning, templates, schedules, change requests"><code>operations.view</code></a> without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Users</td> <td>Administrator</td> <td>The foot of the sidebar (a read-only list), for holders of <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-view" title="View users — See the user list"><code>users.view</code></a> without <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a></td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>Plugin Studio, Report Studio and Lua Studio need no fallback since 2026-10-23: none of them is inside Administrator any more, so each follows only its own Studio permission, wherever you are.</p> <h3 id="fortiweb-adom">FortiWeb ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#fortiweb-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>The device menu is the <strong>FortiWeb</strong> group:</p> <ul> <li><strong>All pages</strong> — a grid with every page of the device's menu, one card per top-level group.</li> <li>FortiWeb's own menu tree, every page SATOM has a GUI layout for on the selected device's build (the layouts arrive with the knowledge packs). <strong>Server Policy</strong> opens SATOM's hand-tuned Server Policy view; every other page opens the measured layout.</li> </ul> <p>With no device selected, or no layout for its build yet, the FortiWeb group holds a single entry, <strong>Server Policy</strong>.</p> <p>Every shared entry is live in the FortiWeb ADOM (Firmware unless an administrator removed the firmware capability in Settings → ADOMs): FortiWeb is the reference menu. The Loadbalancer, WAF and Configuration groups of earlier releases are gone; <strong>Search Attack ID</strong>, <strong>Exceptions & Signature</strong> and <strong>WAF Artifacts</strong> are under <strong>Operations → WAF</strong>, and the old pages still open from a bookmark.</p> <h3 id="fortigate-adom">FortiGate ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#fortigate-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Operations</strong> starts with <strong>Dashboard</strong> (<code>/fgt/</code>), the only device ADOM with a Dashboard entry.</li> <li>The device menu is the <strong>FortiGate</strong> group: <strong>All pages</strong>, the FortiOS menu measured on the selected unit's build, and <strong>Not in GUI, but in CLI</strong> (see <a href="not-in-gui.html">Not in GUI, but in CLI</a>). With no unit selected, or no layout for its build, there is no FortiGate group; the Dashboard lists the section pages.</li> <li><strong>Live:</strong> Migration Report, Naming, Network Segments, Custom Views and Plugin Studio, plus every entry that is live everywhere.</li> <li><strong>Greyed out:</strong> Backend Reachability, Config Compare, every Operations entry, Upgrade Flow, Automations, System Provisioning, Capacity Limits, Firmware (by default), Signatures, Template Library and Lua Studio. Fleet Objects and WAF are not drawn.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="fortigate.html">FortiGate</a>.</p> <h3 id="fortiadc-adom">FortiADC ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#fortiadc-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ul> <li>The device menu is the <strong>FortiADC</strong> group: <strong>All pages</strong>, the FortiADC menu measured on the selected appliance's build, <strong>Not in GUI, but in CLI</strong>, and <strong>Signatures</strong> (SATOM's live signature-policy overview, for holders of <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#protection-view" title="View protection — Browse WAF profiles, signatures, exceptions"><code>protection.view</code></a>).</li> <li>With no appliance selected, or no layout for its build, the FortiADC group holds <strong>Signatures</strong> only. The hand-made FortiADC menu groups of earlier releases are no longer drawn; an old address opens the measured page that shows the same objects, where the selected appliance has one.</li> <li><strong>Live:</strong> Device Backups, Migration Report, Automations, Firmware, Naming, Network Segments, Signatures, Template Library and every Plugins entry, plus every entry that is live everywhere.</li> <li><strong>Greyed out:</strong> Operations → WAF, Backend Reachability, Config Compare, Log Collection, Import Backup, Upgrade Flow, System Provisioning and Capacity Limits.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="fortiadc.html">FortiADC</a>.</p> <h3 id="fortiauthenticator-adom">FortiAuthenticator ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#fortiauthenticator-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ul> <li>The device menu is the <strong>FortiAuthenticator</strong> group: <strong>All pages</strong>, the unit's menu measured on its build, and <strong>Not in GUI, but in CLI</strong>. With no unit selected, or no layout for its build, there is no FortiAuthenticator group; the dashboard lists the section pages.</li> <li><strong>Live:</strong> Automations, Naming, Network Segments, Custom Views and Plugin Studio, plus every entry that is live everywhere.</li> <li><strong>Greyed out:</strong> Backend Reachability, Config Compare, every Operations entry, Upgrade Flow, Migration Report, System Provisioning, Capacity Limits, Firmware (by default), Signatures, Template Library and Lua Studio. Fleet Objects and WAF are not drawn.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="fortiauthenticator.html">FortiAuthenticator</a>.</p> <h3 id="fortianalyzer-adom">FortiAnalyzer ADOM<a class="dc-anchor" href="#fortianalyzer-adom" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ul> <li>The device menu is the <strong>FortiAnalyzer</strong> group when a layout exists for the selected unit's build: <strong>All pages</strong>, the unit's measured menu and <strong>Not in GUI, but in CLI</strong>.</li> <li>Otherwise the sidebar draws SATOM's curated FortiAnalyzer groups instead: <strong>Device Manager</strong>, <strong>FortiView</strong>, <strong>Log View</strong>, <strong>Fabric View</strong>, <strong>Incidents & Events</strong>, <strong>FortiAI</strong>, <strong>Reports</strong> and <strong>System Settings</strong> (never both).</li> <li><strong>Live:</strong> Automations, Firmware (by default), Naming, Network Segments, Custom Views and Report Studio, plus every entry that is live everywhere.</li> <li><strong>Greyed out:</strong> Backend Reachability, Config Compare, every Operations entry, Upgrade Flow, Migration Report, System Provisioning, Capacity Limits, Signatures, Template Library and Lua Studio. Fleet Objects and WAF are not drawn.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="fortianalyzer.html">FortiAnalyzer</a>.</p> <div class="dc-co dc-co-tip"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">💡</span>Tip</p> <p>Administrators can hide live-monitor pages, pages managed on the device and GUI-only pages from every measured device menu under <strong>Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus</strong>. See <a href="settings-adom-menus.html">ADOM Menus</a>.</p> </div> <p>An ADOM that an administrator adds in Settings → ADOMs without a menu of its own shows <strong>‹ Global</strong>, a group named after the ADOM with its <strong>Dashboard</strong>, and <strong>Automation</strong>.</p> <h3 id="bottom-of-the-sidebar">Bottom of the sidebar<a class="dc-anchor" href="#bottom-of-the-sidebar" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Users</strong> — a read-only user list, for holders of <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-view" title="View users — See the user list"><code>users.view</code></a> who do not have the administrator capability (administrators find <strong>Users</strong> under <strong>Administrator</strong>).</li> <li><strong>Settings</strong> — administrators only. Your own Security and Change Password are on your <strong>Profile</strong> (user menu, top right).</li> </ul> <h2 id="other-ways-to-move-around">Other ways to move around<a class="dc-anchor" href="#other-ways-to-move-around" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Breadcrumb</strong> — most pages show <code>Home / …</code> above the title.</li> <li><strong><a href="bookmarks.html">Bookmarks</a></strong> — the star tab on the right edge.</li> <li><strong><a href="concept-map.html">Concept Map</a></strong> — the footer link: every page grouped by what it is for.</li> <li><strong><a href="global-home.html">Global home</a></strong> — the <strong>Global sections</strong> buttons jump to fleet-wide pages.</li> </ul> <h2 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting<a class="dc-anchor" href="#troubleshooting" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <h3 id="a-menu-entry-a-colleague-has-is-missing-for-me">A menu entry a colleague has is missing for me<a class="dc-anchor" href="#a-menu-entry-a-colleague-has-is-missing-for-me" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — your profile lacks the permission behind the group or entry (entries are hidden when you could not open the page), or an administrator switched the feature off (for example Path Diagnostics shows greyed out with <em>"Path Diagnostics is switched off for this site"</em>).</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — compare profiles in <a href="users-and-profiles.html">Users and profiles</a>.</p> <h3 id="i-cannot-find-appliances-system-automations-schema-builds-or-certificate-manager">I cannot find Appliances, System Automations, Schema builds or Certificate Manager<a class="dc-anchor" href="#i-cannot-find-appliances-system-automations-schema-builds-or-certificate-manager" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the entries moved in 3.1.0 and on 2026-10-14. With the administrator capability, <strong>Appliances</strong> is under <strong>Administrator</strong> and <strong>System Automations</strong> under <strong>Administrator → System</strong>; with write access, <strong>Schema builds</strong> and <strong>Build compatibility</strong> are under <strong>Automation → API</strong> (without write access, in the <strong>API</strong> group, or the <strong>API</strong> sub-menu of the <strong>Global</strong> block in the Global ADOM); <strong>Certificate Manager</strong> is under <strong>Automation</strong> (Operations › Automation in a device ADOM); it needs <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#users-manage" title="Manage users — Create, edit, delete, reset and re-profile users"><code>users.manage</code></a>, and it is greyed out in the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs because SATOM manages certificates on FortiWeb and FortiADC only.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — open the group named above, or, if your profile cannot see it, look in <strong>Operations</strong> (the <strong>Global</strong> block in the Global ADOM). See <a href="#when-your-profile-cannot-see-a-group">When your profile cannot see a group</a>.</p> <h3 id="i-cannot-find-scout-ai-advisor-backend-reachability-or-config-compare">I cannot find Scout, AI Advisor, Backend Reachability or Config Compare<a class="dc-anchor" href="#i-cannot-find-scout-ai-advisor-backend-reachability-or-config-compare" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the entries moved and two were renamed on 2026-10-14. Backend Reachability and Config Compare moved into the one shared <strong>Troubleshooting</strong> sub-menu (and left the flat Global list); the fault-localisation ladder formerly called <strong>Scout</strong> is now <strong>Path Diagnostics</strong>; the AI assistant formerly called <strong>AI Advisor</strong> is now <strong>Scout</strong>.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — open <strong>Operations → Troubleshooting</strong> (the <strong>Global</strong> block in the Global ADOM). Scout, the AI assistant, is listed only when you hold <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#advisor-use" title="Use Scout — Chat with Scout, the AI assistant: WAF false-positive triage, Lua drafting, report search"><code>advisor.use</code></a> and an administrator has configured it (Settings → AI → Scout → Providers: <strong>Enable Scout</strong> plus a usable provider). Path Diagnostics does not depend on that: it does not use Scout's AI.</p> <p><strong>Verification</strong> — the sub-menu shows Backend Reachability, Config Compare, Path Diagnostics and, with the permission, Scout (in the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs, Scout only).</p> <h3 id="a-menu-entry-is-greyed-out">A menu entry is greyed out<a class="dc-anchor" href="#a-menu-entry-is-greyed-out" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the page behind it does not work for the devices of this ADOM (for example <strong>Operations → WAF</strong> in FortiADC), or Path Diagnostics is switched off.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — hover the entry to read the reason. Use the ADOM the reason points to (for the WAF pages, FortiWeb), or ask an administrator to switch Path Diagnostics on (Settings → AI → Scout → Path Diagnostics).</p> <h3 id="the-sidebar-shows-a-different-product-than-i-expected">The sidebar shows a different product than I expected<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-sidebar-shows-a-different-product-than-i-expected" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the ADOM is remembered per browser tab; this tab is in a different ADOM.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — check the <strong>ADOM:</strong> badge and use <strong>‹ Global</strong> or <strong>Switch Product</strong>. See <a href="adoms-and-products.html">ADOMs and products</a>.</p> <h3 id="a-column-i-need-is-missing-from-a-table">A column I need is missing from a table<a class="dc-anchor" href="#a-column-i-need-is-missing-from-a-table" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>The window is too narrow for every column, so SATOM hid the least useful ones (see <a href="#wide-tables-and-row-actions">Wide tables and row actions</a>). Click <em>N columns hidden · Show all</em> above the table, widen the window, or collapse the sidebar. An action that is not on the row is in its <strong>…</strong> menu.</p> <h3 id="device-sub-menus-show-select-a-device">Device sub-menus show "Select a device"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#device-sub-menus-show-select-a-device" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — click the device area in the top bar (or <strong>Device</strong> in the sidebar) and pick an appliance.</p></article> <div class="dc-tags"><a class="dc-tag" href="search.html?q=navigation">#navigation</a><a class="dc-tag" href="search.html?q=sidebar">#sidebar</a><a class="dc-tag" The transaction tracer is now a page under Operations → Troubleshooting.</span></a><a class="dc-rel" href="first-login.html"><b>First login, your profile and signing out</b><span>How to sign in (local or directory account), complete two-factor authentication, recover a forgotten password, set your language and other personal preferences, and sign out.</span></a><a class="dc-rel"
